title: plugin-security, plugin-sharing: at boot, the administrator is told when an upgrade renamed, removed or collided with an access choice (#24446 U1)
body:
Part of #24446

U1 of #24446: the access-class upgrade comparison and its boot report. It works to the measurement in 6353200007 and the seat's GO in 6353222762, under claim 6353092498. U2, the marketplace refusal, follows as a separate PR. The ADR-0126 dated note is a separate Tier H docs PR that the seat cuts.

Clause-②: yes (widening: plugin-sharing's exported `SharingRuleService` gains `listDeclaredRules()`; the report itself refuses nothing and adds no key, code or setting)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

**`plugin-security`: `access-upgrade-report.ts` (new), wired at `kernel:bootstrapped` beside `catalog-reference-report.ts`.** At every boot it compares the customer's access state with the registry this boot registered. The customer's state is the activation-ledger rows, the permission sets and positions this system authored (`_provenance: 'org'`, clones included), and the `sys_sharing_rule` rows. It covers sharing rules, permission sets, positions and capabilities, and lists:

1. **Orphans:** ledger rows of type `position`, `permission` or `sharing_rule` whose name the registry no longer resolves.
2. **Suspected re-enablements:** a switched-off orphan whose recorded `package_id` is P, with every name of the same type that P now ships and no ledger row covers. A permission-set candidate names the positions whose definition binds it, which are the acceptance's "affected positions".
3. **Sharing-rule collisions, per organization:** a `sys_sharing_rule` row that holds a declared rule's name. Position, permission-set and capability collisions are already refused at registration or at boot (`security-catalog-namespace.ts`), so a boot that reaches this report holds none of them.
4. **Broken references in the customer's items:**
   - an environment-authored permission set that names an object, a field or a capability the registry lacks. A capability counts as known when it is registered or a package-shipped set still carries it, ADR-0066 ⑨'s rule. This is the capability type's whole part, because capabilities are code-only and never switched;
   - a `sys_sharing_rule` row that names an object or a criteria field the registry lacks.
5. **Field denies a customer set lacks:** a package-shipped set denies a field (`readable: false`, or not `editable` on an object it grants edit on), and an environment-authored set grants the same object with no entry for that field.

It writes nothing and refuses nothing. It follows `catalog-reference-report.ts`'s fail-closed shape:
- a scan, catalog read or declared-rule read that throws stops the report, and nothing is judged from it;
- an absent ledger object, sharing-rule object or sharing service is named in `absent`, and no `sharing_rule` row is judged without the declared-rule list.

**Who is told.** The log gets one line per category, as now. The existing notification ingress, `messaging.emit()` (ADR-0030), also gets one `security.access_upgrade` event with `severity: 'warning'`. It appears in Setup → Diagnostics → Notification Events and in the in-app inbox. No object, page, route or setting is added.
- **`single`:** the Default Organization's `admin_full_access` holders and any `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` address.
- **`group` / `isolated`:** no emit. One `error` line is addressed to the operator, because the notification family is organization-scoped (ADR-0131 D9; the seat's option A, 6353787407). The ledger and the catalog are deployment-level, and under a wall only the operator may switch or clone (ADR-0126 §5, ADR-0131 D3). A tenant administrator is never the fallback.
- **`dedupKey`** is the finding set's digest, so an unchanged set notifies once, not at every boot.
- **No messaging service, no recipient, or a failed emit:** one error line says the findings reached no administrator and names the fix.
- **Mandatory (the seat's question):** not set. The ingress has no per-emit mandatory flag, so a recipient's mute hides it. Making it mute-proof without a new setting means adding `security.access_upgrade` to the messaging plugin's existing `mandatoryTopics` option. The changeset says so.

**`plugin-sharing`: `SharingRuleService.listDeclaredRules()`.** It answers every declared rule with its `packageId`. It answers `null` when the service reads no declarations, which is no answer about any name. plugin-security reaches it as the `sharingRules` service through a structural type and gains no dependency.

## Two limits (accepted by the seat, 6353222762)

Both follow from ADR-0126 §9, under which a clone records no base, no package and no link, and from the bare `(metadata_type, name)` ledger key with its unread `package_id`:
- **A re-enablement is suspected.** Nothing records which name replaced which, and the ledger keeps no version, so "arrived" can only mean "shipped now by P with no ledger row". A package with several unswitched names yields several candidates.
- **The field-deny check reads "grants the same object", not "copied from that set".** It may name an unrelated customer set, so it is a review item.
- **"The old name carrying a clone" is carried by the switch-off half.** The sanctioned ceremony is clone plus switch-off, and a clone whose base stays on is not a choice a rename un-makes. So the acceptance's "switched off or cloned" case is met through the switch-off half. The seat reads this as within ruling 6259332195's intent, not a change to it.

## Scope held

- `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` is unchanged. It is read-only while #25248 is open, and this PR only imports `readDefaultOrganizationId` from it.
- Not `packages/cloud-connection/**` (U2), not `docs/adr/**`, and no `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_SHAPE_GENERATION` change.

## Tests

- `access-upgrade-report.test.ts`: per access type (permission set, position, sharing rule, capability), under `single` and walled, each with a CONTROL that raises nothing. It also covers clone bodies, the fail-closed stops, and delivery: the dedup key, no messaging service, no operator under a wall, a failed emit, and one log line per category.
- `access-upgrade-report.wiring.test.ts`: the acceptance end to end on a real `ObjectQL` engine with `SecurityPlugin` started, under `single`, `isolated` and `group`, with CONTROLs.
- Ablations, each red and then restored:
  - dropping the re-enablement finding turns 10 pins red;
  - letting a walled posture resolve the `single` audience turns 7 red;
  - judging every package-less set as customer-authored turns the stack-set CONTROL red.

The proof readings are in the os-dev-report on #24446: CI, dispatch gates, `check-governed-merges --branch`, R1, R4 under `isolated` and `group`, and the upgrade harness.
